summary: Reviewed mcp-server/tests/utils/workflow-manifest.test.ts — the sole artifact from WP-006. File confirmed passing independently (34/34 tests, 108 ms). Review covers all four dimensions: Maintainability, Best Practices, Security/Performance, and Future Context.

Maintainability: Exemplary. Five clearly delimited describe blocks (roles, pipelines, statuses, constants, derived-constant parity) each own their concern. Variable names are precise (pipelineToRole, inDegree, validIds). Failure messages on every assertion eliminate guesswork when a test breaks.

Best Practices: Correctly uses createRequire for JSON import — matching the pattern established in constants.ts and pipeline-maps.ts. Dynamic async import() in parity tests correctly handles ESM module resolution without circular-import risks. Tests are structural invariants, not value snapshots, so they will not require updates as values evolve — they will _catch_ divergence instead.
Security & Performance: No concerns. Kahn's algorithm is the standard O(V+E) cycle-detection approach and is implemented correctly. JSON loaded once at module level, not per test.

Future Context: The derived-constant parity section is architecturally significant — it creates a living contract binding six exported constants (AGENT_ROLES, ORCHESTRATING_ROLES, PIPELINE_TYPES, DEFAULT_PIPELINE_STAGES, PIPELINE_AGENT_MAP, MAX_REWORK_COUNT, STALE_PIPELINE_HOURS, SPEC_VERSION) directly to manifest values. Any future manifest edit that breaks a consumer will fail the test suite immediately.

One non-blocking observation carried forward from QA: resolveFailAgent() in pipeline-maps.ts retains a hardcoded baseAgentMap parallel to manifest.pipelines.fail_routing. This map is semantically correct today but is not covered by the parity suite and will not auto-propagate on manifest changes. Recommend a follow-on WP to replace it with manifest.pipelines.fail_routing + _roleById lookup — scoped separately.

comments.note: The sequential-number test (role numbers are sequential starting from 1) is not in the WP requirements but is a valuable bonus invariant. This kind of pro-active guard is exactly what a regression file should contain.

WP spec's Files section said 'No new files created' but the developer correctly added the manifest test file per the Requirements section ('Add or verify a test that validates...'). The Files section was a placeholder, not a constraint. The deviation is positive — no concern.

resolveFailAgent() in mcp-server/src/utils/pipeline-maps.ts (line 250) contains a hardcoded baseAgentMap that uses role names ('Developer', 'Release Engineer', 'Documentation') rather than resolving from manifest.fail_routing via the _roleById lookup already in scope. The current values match semantically, but this map will not auto-propagate if manifest fail_routing changes. The parity test suite does not cover resolveFailAgent(). Recommend a dedicated follow-on WP to replace baseAgentMap with: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(workflowManifest.pipelines.fail_routing).map(([p, id]) => [p, _roleById[id]])).
